words.desc: The branch of mathematics that uses letters and symbols to stand for numbers.
The school subject where pupils draw, paint and make creative works.
A gathering of the whole school in one hall to hear news and messages.
A bound collection of charts showing the countries and regions of the world.
A record of which pupils are present at school or in class each day.
A large room with rows of seats facing a stage, used for performances and talks.
A device that rings loudly to mark the start and end of lessons.
The science that studies living organisms and how they grow and function.
A large dark panel on a classroom wall that teachers write on with chalk.
A large school dining area where pupils queue with trays to collect meals.
An electronic device that quickly works out sums and other arithmetic.
The grounds and buildings of a university or college.
A soft white stick of powdery rock used for writing on dark surfaces.
The science of substances, what they are made of and how they react.
A space inside a school where a teacher instructs a group of learners.
A hinged instrument with two arms, used to draw neat round shapes on paper.
A stick of tinted wax used by children to draw pictures.
A formal discussion in which opposing sides argue about a topic.
A punishment where a pupil must stay at school after hours.
A reference volume listing the words of a language together with what they mean.
An official document awarded to someone who has completed a course of study.
A building where students live in shared rooms while at college.
The school subject that teaches reading, writing and the analysis of books and poems.
A small block of rubber used to remove pencil marks from paper.
A structured piece of writing that argues or explains a view on a topic.
A formal assessment of knowledge taken in silence under timed conditions.
An outing where a class travels somewhere new to learn outside the classroom.
The school subject about the planet's lands, climates, peoples and places.
The branch of mathematics that studies shapes, sizes, angles and space.
A spherical model of the Earth that spins on a tilted stand.
A tube of solid adhesive that is twisted up and rubbed onto paper.
A letter or number given to show how good a piece of schoolwork is.
A timetabled period in which pupils exercise and play team games.
A large indoor space with a wooden floor used for physical exercise and games.
A permit that lets a pupil leave the classroom during a lesson.
A pen with bright see-through ink used to mark important text.
The school subject that examines past events, people and civilizations.
Tasks set by teachers for pupils to complete outside of lessons.
The first class young children attend, focused on play and early learning.
A workspace equipped for carrying out scientific experiments and research.
A long talk given by an expert to teach a large group of students.
A small metal cabinet with a door, used by pupils to store their belongings.
A small container for carrying a packed meal to school or work.
A pen with a thick felt tip that draws bold lines in ink.
The school subject that studies numbers, shapes, quantities and patterns.
The school subject where pupils learn to sing, play instruments and read notes.
A bound pad of lined paper pages used for writing things down.
A thin wooden writing tool with a dark core whose marks can be rubbed out.
A paper that a parent signs to let their child take part in a school activity.
The science of matter, energy, motion and the forces that act on them.
A talk given to an audience to share information or ideas.
A piece of extended school study done over several weeks, often in a group.
A formal dance held for older pupils near the end of their final year.
A semicircular tool marked in degrees for measuring and drawing angles.
A short round of questions used to check what someone has learned.
A short pause in the school day when pupils go outside to play.
A document sent home that shows a pupil's grades and a teacher's comments.
A straight flat strip marked with units, used for drawing lines and checking lengths.
Money awarded to a student to help pay for their education.
A large yellow vehicle that carries children between home and school.
The school subject that explores how the natural world works through experiments.
A school event where pupils display their own experiments and projects for judging.
One of the two halves into which a college's teaching calendar is divided.
A small device with a blade that shaves wood to give a pencil a point.
A contest where pupils are knocked out one by one for getting a word wrong.
An annual school event where pupils compete in races and athletic games.
A person who is enrolled at a school or college in order to learn.
A standard volume of lessons and exercises for learning a school subject.
The money charged by a school or college in return for teaching.
An institution of higher learning where students study for degrees.
A period of time away from school or work spent resting or traveling.
A glossy white panel written on with markers whose ink wipes away easily.
